result.instructions: Records GPU use on Apple silicon with Metal System Trace, and native Windows programs with PresentMon. A metal-gpu-trace.json in the repository gives each project its own recordings folder; project_info says which project is active. One recording runs at a time; keep other GPU work off the Mac while it records, and keep the program's window visible: a hidden window stops presenting, and the work after that is left out of the frames (gpu.unpresented; perf_gate fails such a run). Under Wine record 30 s or more: Wine's start-up takes part of the recording. A recording needs about 0.8 GB of free disk per second for Instruments' temporary files (26 GB for 30 s, 50 GB for 60 s); perf_record refuses to start without it. Reading a recording back takes 1 to 14 s per recorded second. Compare only recordings with 100 frames or more, and repeat a run before calling a change real. perf_baseline (or perf_baseline_record, which records them) saves several equal runs as a named reference and perf_check says whether a new run regressed against their range. perf_diagnose says whether a run splits its GPU work into too many short encoders, as translation layers do; perf_compare says how much two runs differ; skip_s on perf_compare and perf_gate leaves out the first seconds (start-up) of each run; perf_history follows FPS, hitches and memory across runs with one name prefix, oldest first; perf_gate says whether a run meets budgets you set (FPS floor, hitch or memory ceiling). trace_tables, trace_count and trace_query read the .trace when KEEP_TRACE=1 kept it, else the run's tables file (<run>.tables.sqlite, written at every recording: perf_runs tables_kept); trace_query's where, columns, order_by, group_by and aggregates filter that file without SQL. When perf_record ends it stops every program of its Wine prefix, or the native program it launched and that program's children. To compare native Metal with a translation layer without a game of one's own: workload_list, workload_fetch, then perf_record with workload and api (and example, for a workload that lists examples), or the compare-layer prompt. The diagnose-stutter prompt tells first-seen shader stutter from steady stutter; bisect-regression finds the commit that slowed a program. perf_sweep records one run per value of dim, example, api or an environment variable and fits GPU ms per frame on the value. trace_query with window_ms sums a long table by time window instead of listing rows. memory_free_pct holds the whole Mac short of memory while recording (keep other work off it) and background throttles the program: repeat a run that uses either. Use tier light to iterate, standard to decide, deep for GPU counters and a kept .trace (METAL_TRACE_MAX_DISK_MB may drop it); compare recordings of the same tier. perf_diagnose and perf_compare return suggested_actions: when it is not empty, run the first one that fits. On a laptop set cooldown_s on perf_baseline_record, perf_ab and perf_sweep so the Mac cools between recordings; a run whose summary has noisy_environment (another process was loading the GPU) is repeated before it is trusted. A recording is refused before it starts when its program, xcrun, the disk or the lock is not ready, or when the screen is locked (METAL_TRACE_ALLOW_LOCKED=1 allows that). When memory spikes or a run stalls, perf_memory_breakdown says which resource types it allocates and drops. A program may write its own numbers to the CSV named in METAL_TRACE_APP_METRICS (first column t_ms, then numeric columns); they come back as the summary's app_metrics, never comparable between programs.

tools.description:
Records `program` (an .exe under Wine, or a macOS binary with wine="native") or a test `workload` for `seconds` with
Metal System Trace and returns its summary: GPU ms per frame, frame intervals, FPS, Metal and resident memory. It
then stops every program of that Wine prefix (wineserver -k), or with native the program it launched and its children.
tier sets memory and counters together; compare recordings of the same tier.

api.description: with workload: mtl, mtl-x64 (Metal under Rosetta), vk (needs METAL_TRACE_MOLTENVK), d3d11 or d3d12 (under wine)

args.description: program arguments as in a shell

background.description: macOS, default false; true throttles the program hard and unevenly (taskpolicy -b): repeat the run

counters.description: default false; true adds gpu_counters; not on Windows; about 40 s of read-back per second

dim.description: with drawstress: cube grid side, dim^3 draws per frame

env.description: NAME=VALUE pairs separated by spaces; MTL_SHADER_VALIDATION=1 or MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1 adds `validation`

example.description: with a workload that lists examples: the one to run

fields.description: result paths to keep, dotted: common.frame_pacing

memory.description: default true; false skips the slowest table, Metal memory (no metal_mib_peak)

memory_free_pct.description: macOS, 20 to 60: holds the whole Mac at this % RAM free while recording; lower can freeze it

prefix.description: Wine prefix, default WINEPREFIX or ~/.wine; ignored with native

program.description: path of the .exe, or of the macOS binary with wine=native

seconds.description: seconds, default 20; 30 under Wine (start-up eats part); the export takes minutes under Wine

size.description: with drawstress: window size, such as 1920x1080

tier.description: default standard. light: no memory or counters; standard: memory; deep: also counters and a kept .trace (macOS). memory and counters given alone override

wine.description: Wine directory holding bin/wine, or native

workdir.description: directory to start in, default the program's own

workload.description: a test program from workload_list (fetch it first) instead of program

tools.name: perf_record
tools.title: Record a program

tools.description:
Records the same program `count` times with perf_record's arguments and saves the runs as the reference `name` for
perf_check, returning the range each number spans. Runs are `name`-1, `name`-2, ... Each takes its seconds plus
about a minute of read-back.

cooldown_s.description: seconds to rest between recordings, 0 to 600, default 0; 60 on a laptop is a start, thermal_state_share says if it throttled

skip_s.description: seconds to leave out at the start (shaders compile, resources load), default 0; GPU numbers, hitches and Metal memory are recomputed without them; perf_check applies the same cut

tools.title: Record a reference

annotations.title: Record one run per value of a variable

tools.description:
Records the same program once per value of one variable and returns, per value, the median FPS, 1 % low, GPU ms per
frame and stutter; with 3 or more numeric values also the line GPU ms follows (fixed ms plus ms per unit) with its
r2. With rounds above 1 the values run in reverse every other round, so drift hits all alike. Runs are `name`-<value
number>-r<round>; each takes its seconds plus about a minute of read-back.

tools.name: perf_runs
tools.title: List recordings

tools.description:
Compares two saved recordings, a the reference and b the run after a change: headline numbers (FPS, GPU ms, frame
pacing, memory), then the GPU work: encoders and command buffers per frame, share of short encoders, idle time, and
each encoder label's change, largest first. `layer` says whether both ran on the same translation layer; `measure`
marks Windows against Metal (use FPS, lows, stutter, jitter); runs under 100 frames are flagged. `screen`,
`noisy_environment` flag runs that do not compare; `suggested_actions` says what to call next.

summaries as the reference, replacing a previous one, and returns each number's range and `spread_pct`: the noise a
change must exceed. With name alone it shows that reference; with nothing it lists them.

Judges a recording against a reference from perf_baseline: regressed when FPS falls under the reference's lowest, or
GPU ms per frame rises over its highest, by more than margin_pct, or encoders or command buffers per frame exceed

content.text:
Compare drawstress in native Metal with drawstress through d3d12 under the Wine in METAL_TRACE_WINE, with the metal-trace tools:
1. workload_fetch name=drawstress (it is skipped when already downloaded).
2. perf_record label=drawstress-mtl workload=drawstress api=mtl seconds=20.
3. perf_record label=drawstress-d3d12 workload=drawstress api=d3d12 seconds=30.
4. perf_compare a=<the mtl run> b=<the other run>, and perf_diagnose on the other run for its verdict.
Report perf_compare's metrics and encoders as one table (a, b, change), then its labels with the largest change in GPU ms per frame, then the verdict. Say which runs are in too_short, and that one pair of runs is not enough to call a difference real: repeat both before concluding.

Function pointers and ray tracing in render pipelines are not compatible with mesh shading.

result.instructions: Records GPU use on Apple silicon with Metal System Trace, and native Windows programs with PresentMon. A metal-gpu-trace.json in the repository gives each project its own recordings folder; project_info says which project is active. One recording runs at a time; keep other GPU work off the Mac while it records, and keep the program's window visible: a hidden window stops presenting, and the work after that is left out of the frames (gpu.unpresented; perf_gate fails such a run). Under Wine record 30 s or more: Wine's start-up takes part of the recording. A recording needs about 0.8 GB of free disk per second for Instruments' temporary files (26 GB for 30 s, 50 GB for 60 s); perf_record refuses to start without it. Reading a recording back takes 1 to 14 s per recorded second. Compare only recordings with 100 frames or more, and repeat a run before calling a change real. perf_baseline (or perf_baseline_record, which records them) saves several equal runs as a named reference and perf_check says whether a new run regressed against their range. perf_diagnose says whether a run splits its GPU work into too many short encoders, as translation layers do; perf_compare says how much two runs differ; skip_s on perf_compare and perf_gate leaves out the first seconds (start-up) of each run; perf_history follows FPS, hitches and memory across runs with one name prefix, oldest first; perf_gate says whether a run meets budgets you set (FPS floor, hitch or memory ceiling). trace_tables, trace_count and trace_query read the .trace when KEEP_TRACE=1 kept it, else the run's tables file (<run>.tables.sqlite, written at every recording: perf_runs tables_kept); trace_query's where, columns, order_by, group_by and aggregates filter that file without SQL. When perf_record ends it stops every program of its Wine prefix, or the native program it launched and that program's children. To compare native Metal with a translation layer without a game of one's own: workload_list, workload_fetch, then perf_record with workload and api (and example, for a workload that lists examples), or the compare-layer prompt. The diagnose-stutter prompt tells first-seen shader stutter from steady stutter; bisect-regression finds the commit that slowed a program. perf_sweep records one run per value of dim, example, api or an environment variable and fits GPU ms per frame on the value. trace_query with window_ms sums a long table by time window instead of listing rows. memory_free_pct holds the whole Mac short of memory while recording (keep other work off it) and background throttles the program: repeat a run that uses either. Use tier light to iterate, standard to decide, deep for GPU counters and a kept .trace (METAL_TRACE_MAX_DISK_MB may drop it); compare recordings of the same tier. perf_diagnose and perf_compare return suggested_actions: when it is not empty, run the first one that fits. On a laptop set cooldown_s on perf_baseline_record, perf_ab and perf_sweep so the Mac cools between recordings; a run whose summary has noisy_environment (another process was loading the GPU) is repeated before it is trusted. A recording is refused before it starts when its program, xcrun, the disk or the lock is not ready, or when the screen is locked (METAL_TRACE_ALLOW_LOCKED=1 allows that). When memory spikes or a run stalls, perf_memory_breakdown says which resource types it allocates and drops. A program may write its own numbers to the CSV named in METAL_TRACE_APP_METRICS (first column t_ms, then numeric columns); they come back as the summary's app_metrics, never comparable between programs.

tools.description:
Records `program` (an .exe under Wine, or a macOS binary with wine="native") or a test `workload` for `seconds` with
Metal System Trace and returns its summary: GPU ms per frame, frame intervals, FPS, Metal and resident memory. It
then stops every program of that Wine prefix (wineserver -k), or with native the program it launched and its children.
tier sets memory and counters together; compare recordings of the same tier.

args.description: program arguments as in a shell

background.description: macOS, default false; true throttles the program hard and unevenly (taskpolicy -b): repeat the run

counters.description: default false; true adds gpu_counters; not on Windows; about 40 s of read-back per second

dim.description: with drawstress: cube grid side, dim^3 draws per frame

env.description: NAME=VALUE pairs separated by spaces; MTL_SHADER_VALIDATION=1 or MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1 adds `validation`

example.description: with a workload that lists examples: the one to run

fields.description: result paths to keep, dotted: common.frame_pacing

memory.description: default true; false skips the slowest table, Metal memory (no metal_mib_peak)

memory_free_pct.description: macOS, 20 to 60: holds the whole Mac at this % RAM free while recording; lower can freeze it

prefix.description: Wine prefix, default WINEPREFIX or ~/.wine; ignored with native

program.description: path of the .exe, or of the macOS binary with wine=native

seconds.description: seconds, default 20; 30 under Wine (start-up eats part); the export takes minutes under Wine

size.description: with drawstress: window size, such as 1920x1080

tier.description: default standard. light: no memory or counters; standard: memory; deep: also counters and a kept .trace (macOS). memory and counters given alone override

wine.description: Wine directory holding bin/wine, or native

workdir.description: directory to start in, default the program's own

workload.description: a test program from workload_list (fetch it first) instead of program
